name: Rotunda-Waste
geological_features: Circular erosion basins with flat floors
specific_features: Trace atmospheric compounds inconsistent with natural planetary chemistry
description: Rotunda-Waste is a barren world whose surface has been scoured to bedrock across most of its area, the thin atmosphere having slowly stripped away regolith and sediment over billions of years. The dominant features are circular erosion basins, shallow depressions with perfectly flat floors where harder rock resisted the wind while softer surrounding material was carried away. These rotunda-like basins range from meters to tens of kilometers across, giving the landscape a pockmarked, used-up appearance.

The thin atmosphere carries enough dust to create a faint haze at ground level, softening the horizon into a murky brown blur. The wind is constant and erosive, polishing exposed rock to a glossy finish that reflects the sky. The basins collect what little dust the wind deposits, their flat floors covered in thin, unstable layers that puff into clouds at the lightest disturbance. The overall impression is of a world that is slowly being erased.

Atmospheric analysis has detected trace compounds, specifically certain noble gas isotope ratios, that are inconsistent with the planet's natural geological history. These anomalies suggest that either the planet received material from an unusual source such as a nearby supernova remnant, or that it was once the site of activity that altered its atmospheric chemistry. No physical evidence of such activity has been found on the surface, and the anomaly remains unexplained.

Rotunda-Waste has minimal resource value and no strategic importance. Its thin atmosphere and flat terrain make it suitable for automated landing sites, but there is nothing here to land for. The atmospheric anomaly has generated some scientific papers but not enough interest to fund a dedicated mission. The planet exists in the catalogs as a note, a barren world with one small mystery that may never be solved.
